inline_comments.comment:
Both `headWatcher` and `packedRefsWatcher` are installed on the same path: `gitDir` (the `.git` directory). Because `node:fs.watch` on a directory fires for any file change directly inside it, a single OS event — such as git writing `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` or updating `.git/index` — triggers both listeners in the same tick, calling `emitGitStateChange()` twice. The downstream debounce in `ChangeDetectionService` absorbs the duplicates, but the double-fire is architecturally surprising and means two debounce timers are reset instead of one.

The two watchers are distinguishable by their `onChange` callback (the `head` watcher also calls `reconfigureBranchWatcher`). Consider using a single directory watcher that checks `filename` (available on most platforms) or consolidate the callbacks into one watcher with branching logic.

`GitDiffProviderTestContext` declares a `mockReadFile` field and `setupGitWatchProvider` returns it, but none of the new test cases in this diff destructure or use it. This is dead API surface on the context object. Either remove the field and return value, or add a test that exercises it (e.g., verifying HEAD-read failures are handled gracefully).

`(node) => void existingNodes.add(node)` uses a concise arrow body where `void` discards the `Set.add()` return value. Biome's `lint/suspicious/useIterableCallbackReturn` rule requires `forEach` callbacks to use block bodies when the expression's value must be suppressed. Use:
```typescript
nodes.forEach((node) => { existingNodes.add(node); });
```

`void callback;` is a no-op expression statement — it evaluates `callback` and discards the result, but doesn't suppress any TypeScript or lint diagnostic (TypeScript does not warn about unused parameters). It will confuse future readers who may wonder what it is supposed to do. Simply remove it; the mock's default implementation is already correct without it.

general_comments.comment: The `gitDiffProvider` option in `ChangeDetectionService` has been narrowed from `Pick<GitDiffProvider, 'getChangedFiles' | 'getRepoRoot'>` (a duck-typed structural type that allowed plain object mocks) to the concrete `GitDiffProvider` class. This is required because `onGitStateChange` must now be part of the contract, but the concrete-class requirement forces every caller — including future external consumers — to subclass `GitDiffProvider` rather than providing a simple adapter object. Consider extracting an `IGitDiffProvider` interface that captures the full three-method contract (`getChangedFiles`, `getRepoRoot`, `onGitStateChange`), and type the option and field against the interface instead. The `MockGitDiffProvider` would still satisfy it via class extension, but plain object mocks would also be possible.

The new `getStoryIdsByAbsolutePath` implementation stores both the original absolute path and the `normalizePath`-ed version as separate keys in `storyIdsByFile`, which is the correct approach for Windows cross-platform compatibility. However, on non-Windows systems where the two values are identical, `addStoryId` is called twice with the same key and story ID — the second call is a no-op but adds unnecessary churn. A short inline comment noting that the dual-key strategy is intentional for Windows path compatibility would help future readers understand why the same story ID appears to be registered twice.
